```{r}
#| include: false
source("site/helpers.R")
```

## Survey base and disruption rate

The 2024 Tunisia wave contains `r evidence$raw_n` establishment records. `r evidence$connected_usable_n` provide a valid yes/no disruption response; `r evidence$no_internet_connection_n` explicitly report having no internet connection. Among the valid connected-business responses, `r evidence$disruption_events` report an internet disruption.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-survey-evidence
#| tbl-cap: "Survey-weighted 2024 internet evidence"
display <- data.frame(
  Metric = c(
    "Valid connected-business responses", "Effective sample size", "Reported disruptions",
    "Weighted disruption rate", "Usable duration responses", "Weighted mean duration",
    "Usable loss-ratio responses", "Positive loss responses"
  ),
  Value = c(
    evidence$connected_usable_n,
    fmt_num(evidence$effective_n),
    evidence$disruption_events,
    fmt_pct(evidence$disruption_rate_weighted),
    evidence$duration_usable_n,
    paste0(fmt_num(evidence$mean_duration_hours_weighted), " hours"),
    evidence$loss_ratio_usable_n,
    evidence$positive_loss_events
  ),
  check.names = FALSE
)
knitr::kable(display, align = c("l", "r"))
```

The raw rate is `r fmt_pct(evidence$disruption_rate_unweighted)`. The weighted estimate is `r fmt_pct(evidence$disruption_rate_weighted)` and is the preferred survey estimate. Neither number is a national network-availability rate: the outcome is a business response over the prior fiscal year.

## Duration construction

WBES records hours and, for interruptions shorter than one hour, minutes. The harmonisation rule is

$$
D_i=
\begin{cases}
H_i, & H_i>0,\\[3pt]
M_i/60, & H_i=0\text{ and }M_i\text{ is observed},\\[3pt]
\text{missing}, & \text{otherwise}.
\end{cases}
$$

This avoids treating an unknown minute response as a zero-duration interruption.

## Provider-switching friction

![Survey-weighted provider-switching responses](artifacts/public/figures/provider-switching.png){fig-alt="Horizontal bar chart of reported difficulty changing internet providers."}

The combined weighted share reporting one provider only, inability to switch, or some difficulty is **`r fmt_pct(evidence$provider_switch_constraint_rate_weighted)`**. This is a resilience indicator, not proof of market power or service failure.

## Loss-cost evidence

```{r}
#| label: tbl-loss-chain
#| tbl-cap: "Actuarial loss-cost components"
display <- data.frame(
  Component = c(
    "Disruption probability", "Positive loss probability | disruption",
    "Mean positive loss ratio", "Expected loss ratio"
  ),
  Estimate = c(
    fmt_pct(calibration$disruption_probability),
    fmt_pct(calibration$positive_loss_probability_given_disruption),
    fmt_ratio_pct(calibration$mean_positive_loss_ratio),
    fmt_ratio_pct(calibration$expected_loss_ratio)
  ),
  check.names = FALSE
)
knitr::kable(display, align = c("l", "r"))
```

The 95% weighted-resampling interval for the expected loss ratio is **`r fmt_ratio_pct(bootstrap$lower_95)` to `r fmt_ratio_pct(bootstrap$upper_95)`**. The interval is wide because the severity tail rests on 16 positive observations.

## Disclosure-screened segments

Only segments with at least 30 usable observations and five disruption events are published.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-segments
#| tbl-cap: "Disclosure-screened segment evidence"
display <- data.frame(
  Dimension = segments$dimension,
  Segment = segments$segment,
  `Raw n` = segments$raw_n,
  `Effective n` = segments$effective_n,
  Events = segments$disruption_events,
  `Weighted rate` = fmt_pct(segments$disruption_rate_weighted),
  check.names = FALSE
)
knitr::kable(display, align = c("l", "l", "r", "r", "r", "r"))
```

Segment labels are survey category codes. Differences are descriptive and do not establish causal effects.
